evidence.note: Wrote and ran a battery of real boto3 test scripts (test2-test7) covering multipart, ranged GET, copy, conditional, presigned GET/PUT, admin API, cross-tenant access denial, bucket policy, versioning, tagging — genuine boto3 round-trips, not assumptions.
boto3 multipart complete failed with InvalidPart; agent debugged to a namespace-aware XML parsing bug, fixed it, restarted and re-ran test2 — verification used to gate a real fix.

Deep SigV4 verification on Unicode/special-char keys: reproduced boto3's canonical-URI encoding, compared computed vs boto3 signatures byte-for-byte, found a WSGI latin-1 path-decode bug, fixed and re-tested — signing verified against the exact client.
Concurrency load test: 200 puts with 40 workers, checked for errors/corruption — reproduces the grader's load/corruption gate.

Console verified via static grep of data-testid count in app.js plus API-level end-to-end calls (login/create/delete key), but NOT driven through a browser/DOM to check visible side-effects (row-add-without-reload, modal, confirm dialog) — the browser-graded UX half is not reproduced.
Signature-failure and error-path tests plus repeated full re-runs of the whole test battery on fresh server state to catch regressions.

reasoning: The agent built a broad, self-authored boto3 verification harness covering header+query signing (including byte-exact SigV4 debugging on Unicode paths), edge behaviors (ranged GET, conditional, error codes), versioning/multipart/tagging, cross-tenant codes, and a 40-worker concurrency load test, and used these checks to gate real fixes and re-ran them as a battery — squarely above anchor 5 and hitting most of anchor 8. It falls short of a full 8/10 because the console — worth half the final score and graded by a browser on visible DOM side-effects — was verified only via static testid grep and API-level calls, never driven through the DOM, so the browser grader's loop was not reproduced. This lands at 7.
